Hi Jill — thanks for sending these over and for the clear redlines. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Naomi (finance) so we can give you an authoritative response on remit entity, VAT, and the payment-term ask.

Short replies to your asks:
- Invoice remit: Redwood Inference invoices from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity) by default, but for EU customers we can invoice from Redwood EU Solutions Ltd. if that helps with VAT handling. Kimberly/Naomi: if GreenScale prefers an EU invoice entity, what evidence do we need to accept that routing for this deal?
- VAT: please send GreenScale's VAT registration number and the tax certificate (we saw a GB cert referenced in your attachment list). If GreenScale is subject to reverse-charge, we will not charge VAT and will include the customer's VAT ID on invoice. Naomi: please confirm invoice flow & whether redwood needs a vendor tax form.

On the commercial asks: we saw the 60-day net request in the redline. Our standard is net30; we can consider a one-off extension to net45 for Strategic customers. Kimberly: is net45 acceptable from a legal/credit perspective if procurement insists? Karthik: tagging you as AE — any commercial flexibility on commits/pricing cadence to justify extended terms?

If it's helpful, I'm available for a 20-minute sync tomorrow between 09:00-11:00 CET. Otherwise, we can handle via email — I can produce a clean order form with our proposed compromises.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form — redlines and VAT question

Diego / team — quick legal read of the customer redlines attached. Key points / proposed positions:

1) Payment terms (customer requested 60 days) — we should push back. Operationally, net30 is the standard; net45 may be approved for enterprise deals with credit review. Recommend: counter with net45 and include an escalation clause that returns to net30 if commercial minimums are not met in first 90 days.

2) Minimum commit language — customer reduced the minimum commit runway in their redline. We should retain the original minimum commit duration but can accept a 10% reduction to the first tranche as a compromise. Add explicit language that unused committed units are non-refundable but can be converted to credits within 12 months.

3) VAT / invoicing entity — if they require an EU invoicing entity, request: (a) VAT registration number, (b) official tax certificate, (c) remit-to legal name and address, and (d) a PO referencing the correct remit entity. If any of (a)-(c) are missing we invoice from US entity and apply US-to-EU VAT rules (i.e., charge VAT where applicable).

I attached inline comments to the redline PDF. If we go net45, finance should run credit terms (Naomi). If finance flags, legal will require a credit hold fallback clause.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form — redlines and VAT question

Diego / Kimberly / Karthik — finance's view on VAT and payment terms:

- VAT: If GreenScale provides a valid EU VAT number (e.g., ITXXXXXXXX), we will not charge Redwood EU Solutions Ltd invoices VAT and will apply reverse-charge language on the invoice. Please confirm the exact VAT ID and upload the GreenScale_TaxCert_GB_2025.pdf (or equivalent).

- Invoice entity: We can invoice from Redwood EU Solutions Ltd for this deal, but we need the following from GreenScale before we switch: remit-to name, legal address, and a signed PO referencing that remit entity.

- Payment terms: net30 is preferred. If we move to net45 as a commercial concession, we need: (a) approval from credit (I will run a quick check), (b) an invoice escalation clause (late fees and suspension rights at 60 days), and (c) a requirement that the first invoice be paid within 30 days to trigger any extended terms thereafter.

I'll start the credit check — if it passes, we can agree net45 with the legal fallback above.

Naomi Feldman

Subject: Finalizing Order Form redlines + next steps for invoicing / VAT

Hi Jill / Procurement — thanks for the redlines and for your patience while we pulled internal approvals together. Summary / next steps below so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Invoicing entity & VAT: please confirm GreenScale's VAT registration number and upload the tax certificate (we saw GreenScale_TaxCert_GB_2025.pdf referenced). If you confirm an Italian VAT ID, Redwood will issue invoices from Redwood EU Solutions Ltd and apply reverse-charge (no VAT on our invoice). If you prefer the US remit entity, we'll invoice Redwood Inference, Inc. and VAT treatment will follow the invoice country rules.

2) Payment terms: Redwood prefers net30. We can agree to net45 as a one-time concession pending a successful credit check by finance. Naomi is running the check now — I'll update you by EOD tomorrow. If credit is approved we will: (a) update the order form to net45, (b) include an escalation clause that reverts to net30 and suspends service after 60 days of non-payment.

3) Minimum commit: legal requests we keep the existing minimum commit duration with a 10% concession on the first tranche. Kimber has attached the redline with proposed language — please review and confirm.

4) PO and remit details: please provide the PO number and remit-to legal entity name and address to ensure invoices route correctly.

If that sounds right, I will prepare a clean order form incorporating (i) net45 if credit checks ok, (ii) the 10% concession on first tranche, and (iii) the invoicing entity based on the VAT evidence you provide. Once you confirm, we'll share the final doc for signature.

Would you like a 30-minute call to walk through these points? I'm available tomorrow 10:00-13:00 CET.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
